title: Placement Test
blurb: 30 items · ~40 minutes · 100 points. One sitting, no dictionary, no AI help. Cheating it only cheats you.

parts.title: Fix the sentence
parts.blurb: Each sentence has at least one error. Rewrite it correctly. 2 points each.

items.answer: I worked as a sales supervisor from 2021 to 2024.

parts.title: Choose the right word
parts.blurb: Pick the word that fits. 2 points each.

items.answer: I have worked here since 2021.
She is good at mathematics.
I am waiting for your reply.
He is interested in data science.
The client sent the file yesterday.

items.answer: I need some information about your pricing.

options: We discussed ___ the project on Monday.

parts.title: Listening & shadowing self-check
parts.blurb: Do each task honestly, then score yourself 1 / 3 / 5. 5 points each.

items.prompt: Shadow the first 30 seconds (repeat 0.5–1 sec behind the speaker). Could you stay with the speaker without long pauses? (5 = yes, smoothly; 3 = mostly, some gaps; 1 = kept losing them)
Transcribe the first full sentence you hear, then check against the transcript or subtitles. What % of words did you get right? (5 = 90%+, 3 = 70–89%, 1 = below 70%)

Say these pairs aloud and record yourself: thin/tin, very/wary, west/vest, day/deh. Listen back. Do the two words in each pair sound clearly different? (5 = all four pairs distinct; 3 = two or three; 1 = they sound the same)

Read this paragraph aloud at natural speed and record it: "I usually start my day with tea and revision. Last month I built a small dashboard for practice, and I have learned a lot since then. The client I want to work with needs clear weekly updates." Listen back. Count your slips (dropped articles, wrong word stress, swallowed endings). (5 = 0–2 slips; 3 = 3–5 slips; 1 = 6+)

parts.title: Speaking
parts.blurb: Record both on your phone. Then score yourself honestly, 2–10 each.

items.title: 2-minute introduction:
items.prompt: Who are you, what do you study, what work do you want to do next? Speak for the full 2 minutes — no reading.
items.scale: Score 2–10 with the 4 lenses (clarity/tone/structure/client-safety). Be strict.

items.title: 90-second client answer:
items.prompt: A client asks, "Tell me about a project you worked on." Answer as yourself, honestly (coursework and practice projects count — real ones only).
items.scale: Score 2–10 with the 4 lenses (clarity/tone/structure/client-safety). Be strict.

parts.title: Writing
parts.blurb: Write your answers, then score yourself 1–5 each.

items.prompt: Write 3 sentences about what you did yesterday (past tense).
items.scale: 5 = clean and client-safe · 3 = understandable with slips · 1 = hard to follow

items.prompt: Write 3 sentences about what you have done this week (present perfect).
items.scale: 5 = clean and client-safe · 3 = understandable with slips · 1 = hard to follow

items.prompt: A client writes: "Can you build a sales dashboard? What do you charge?" Reply in under 60 words. (No price yet — never price before scope.)
items.scale: 5 = clean and client-safe · 3 = understandable with slips · 1 = hard to follow

items.prompt: Describe your typical day in 5 English sentences.
items.scale: 5 = clean and client-safe · 3 = understandable with slips · 1 = hard to follow

bands.note: You can handle simple, familiar topics. Client calls are not yet safe — that is exactly what this course fixes.
You survive everyday English. The course takes you to B2: independent, client-ready.
You are closer than you think — use the course as a tune-up, especially Modules 5–7.
